title: Beluga: A CXL-Based Memory Architecture for Scalable and Efficient LLM KVCache Management
event_hint: Architecture lets GPUs and CPUs share a large memory pool via CXL switches, cutting KVCache TTFT by 89.6% and boosting vLLM throughput 7.35x versus RDMA-based disaggregated memory (SIGPOST'26).
problem: Growing LLM model sizes and long-context inference make GPU/HBM memory a critical bottleneck, forcing reliance on host DRAM; but per-CPU memory channels cap DRAM capacity. Existing RDMA-based disaggregated memory pools suffer high access latency, complex communication protocols, and synchronization overhead.
mechanism: Beluga enables GPUs and CPUs to access a shared, large-scale memory pool through CXL switches, aiming for near-local memory latency with reduced protocol complexity. It includes Beluga-KVCache, a component for managing large-scale KVCache in LLM inference, and claims to be the first system letting GPUs directly access large-scale memory pools through CXL switches.

evidence.claim: 89.6% reduction in Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) compared to RDMA-based disaggregated memory solutions.
7.35x throughput improvement in the vLLM inference engine compared to RDMA-based solutions.
Beluga is the first system that enables GPUs to directly access large-scale memory pools through CXL switches.

evaluation_context: Quantitative gains measured against RDMA-based disaggregated memory baselines within the vLLM inference engine; work accepted to SIGPOST'26. Model sizes, workload traces, CXL generation, and switch topology details reside in the full paper (not fetched).
limitations: Abstract-level results only; full body not fetched, so workload specifics, model/context lengths, CXL device generation, scalability limits, and cost analysis are unverified. 'Near-local memory latency' is a qualitative claim without a numeric figure in the abstract. The 'first system' claim should be checked against concurrent CXL-GPU-direct work.
project_relevance: Directly on-topic for the briefing's CXL/disaggregated-memory and KVCache-management interests: Beluga is a CXL-switch-based memory pool designed for LLM KVCache, the same workload class as cross-node KVCache transfer, and positions itself as an RDMA alternative. The GPU-direct-access-over-CXL angle is relevant to DPU/SmartNIC-offload comparisons and to inference-network memory tiers.
